Kim, Jordan — attached is the first pass of the canonical network diagram (see attachment stub). Key callouts in the diagram:

- Control-plane (orange): managed control-plane endpoints are in a separate management VPC with private peering to Dedicated pools. Control-plane traffic between orchestrator and inference nodes uses mTLS and is restricted to specific subnets.
- Data-plane (green): tenant inference traffic is confined to tenant-specific subnets/VLANs. For Private deployments we provision per-customer VPCs with dedicated route tables; Dedicated pools use logical tenant segmentation plus hypervisor-level isolation.
- Inter-enclave routing: implemented via policy-based routing at the virtual router and enforced by service-level ACLs; only allowed flows are model fetching (443), metrics (TCP 9000), and KV-cache replication (TLS 54321).

Summary (high level):
- Boundary diagram: see VERDANT_enclave_comm_diagram_v2.pdf. Control-plane is isolated in a management VPC and uses mutual TLS between control components; data-plane (tenant inference) is placed into tenant-specific subnets with enforced ACLs.

Certificates are issued by our internal PKI and keys are managed in customer-configurable KMS/HSM for Private deployments.
- Egress and monitoring: egress is filtered via a managed egress appliance with multi-tier filtering (allowlist + DPI) for Private deployments. Flow logs and connection metadata are forwarded to our observability stack for anomaly detection.
